title: Postmortem: Cart Redis primary failover caused elevated errors
body: A Redis primary backing the Cart Service (APP-004) failed over under organic memory pressure, causing a ~9 minute spike in cart write errors in NA while a replica was promoted and clients reconnected. Root cause was capacity: insufficient headroom plus a slow client connection-pool reconnect tail. Fixed operationally via the designed Sentinel promotion; follow-ups add proactive capacity alerting, tuned reconnect intervals, and quarterly Redis sizing reviews.

title: Postmortem: Guest checkout created orphaned loyalty accounts
body: PR-0207 wired the Checkout Service (APP-003) to provision a Loyalty (APP-015) account on every order placement, including guest orders, violating the invariant that guest carts must not create loyalty accounts (KN-045) and producing orphaned accounts across NA and EU. Root cause was a code regression plus a test gap (no negative assertion) and dropped loyalty domain rules in context. Fixed by hotfix PR-0312 (story CHK-1421), which gated provisioning on an authenticated identity and added the negative test; the lesson became EXP-090.

title: Postmortem: Search reindex lag surfaced stale prices in results
body: REL-2026-002 changed catalog-to-index propagation cadence, increasing latency so the Search & Browse (APP-006) index briefly showed stale prices in NA search results. Root cause was a data-freshness (propagation lag) issue, not incorrect data; authoritative price resolution at cart/checkout prevented any mischarge. Resolved self-healing as the reindex backlog drained; follow-ups right-size propagation cadence and add a pre-release freshness-impact check.

title: Postmortem: Regional price rule misconfiguration in APAC
body: A regional rounding-rule configuration change in REL-2026-003 set the wrong rounding direction for APAC, producing systematic off-by-one minor-unit rounding in resolved prices (APP-007) for ~22 minutes. Root cause was a config change that reached production without per-region rounding-invariant validation. Fixed by rolling the configuration back to the prior known-good value; follow-ups add automated rounding-invariant assertions and staged validation for regional pricing config.

title: Postmortem: Promotion-window price change did not invalidate promo cache
body: First of the promo-cache-staleness trio: during REL-2026-004 a promotion-window price change in Pricing (APP-007) did not invalidate the Promotions Engine (APP-008) cache, so stale promo data produced incorrect cart totals at checkout (APP-003) across NA and EU (Sev1). Root cause was cache staleness: TTL-based invalidation with no event-driven flush on upstream price change. Mitigated by a promo-cache flush and a targeted path-specific invalidation; the tactical fix later proved insufficient (see INC-2026-011, INC-2026-018) and seeds KN-063.

title: Postmortem: Primary PSP degraded; authorization latency spiked
body: MCG's primary external payment service provider degraded, spiking Payments (APP-012) authorization p99 and causing slow/failed auths in NA and LATAM until failover engaged. Root cause was third-party degradation, worsened by a manual (non-automatic) PSP failover step; PCI boundaries held and idempotency keys prevented double-charges. Resolved by failing over to the secondary PSP; follow-ups automate health-based failover and tune circuit breakers.

title: Postmortem: Promo cache staleness recurrence during flash sale
body: Second of the promo-cache-staleness trio: during a flash sale the Promotions Engine (APP-008) again served stale promo data, causing brief cart-total mismatches at checkout (APP-003) in NA. Root cause was the same cache staleness as INC-2026-007; the post-incident targeted invalidation did not cover the rapid activation/deactivation path. Mitigated by a promo-cache flush and escalated toward a systemic write-through fix, ultimately delivered in INC-2026-018.

title: Postmortem: ATP oversell on multi-warehouse SKUs
body: REL-2026-006 introduced a reservation path in the Inventory Service (APP-010) that did not serialize decrements for multi-warehouse SKUs, allowing a read-modify-write race that briefly oversold high-demand items so Order Management (APP-009) accepted unfulfillable orders in NA. Root cause was a data-consistency defect in reservation semantics under concurrency. Mitigated by serializing decrements (per-SKU guard); follow-ups harden atomic reservation and add concurrency tests.

title: Postmortem: Rate-limit threshold too aggressive after rollout
body: REL-2026-007 shipped a token-bucket rate-limit configuration to the API Gateway (APP-024) with a threshold too low for EU traffic, rejecting legitimate requests with HTTP 429 for ~14 minutes. Root cause was a config change deployed without validation against observed regional traffic baselines. Fixed by rolling back the rate-limit configuration; follow-ups derive thresholds from per-region baselines and add a canary stage for rate-limit changes.

title: Postmortem: Edge OIDC verification rejected valid tokens
body: A REL-2026-007 change to edge OIDC verification in the API Gateway (APP-024), validating Identity (APP-014) tokens, applied too tight a clock-skew tolerance, so edge nodes with minor clock offset rejected valid tokens and intermittently signed out NA and EU users. Root cause was deployment-shaped: the failure manifested non-uniformly by node clock offset and was not reproduced in a clock-synchronized test environment. Fixed by rolling back the verification change; follow-ups add a configurable skew tolerance, NTP drift monitoring, and skew-injection tests. The failure was in the safe direction (no invalid token accepted).

title: Postmortem: Self-service returns showed incorrect eligibility
body: REL-2026-008 introduced a boundary-condition regression in the Customer Portal (APP-021) returns-eligibility rule, marking some genuinely returnable NA orders as ineligible for self-service return for ~30 minutes. Root cause was a code regression (inclusive/exclusive comparison on the return window) with no boundary test coverage; the error was over-restrictive and support-assisted returns remained available. Fixed by reverting the rule; follow-ups add boundary tests and a returns golden-case suite.

title: Postmortem: Storefront latency degradation under load test
body: A pre-peak load test saturated the Storefront Web origin (APP-001) while the API Gateway (APP-024) passed full load through, degrading p95/p99 latency for a fraction of NA users overlapping the test window. Root cause was capacity: insufficient origin autoscaling headroom and edge load-shedding not pre-configured to protect the origin. Mitigated by tuning edge load-shedding; follow-ups right-size origin headroom and schedule load tests off-peak with better isolation.

title: Postmortem: Third promo-cache staleness incident triggers systemic fix
body: Third and final promo-cache-staleness incident (after INC-2026-007 and INC-2026-011): the Promotions Engine (APP-008) again served stale promo data, causing incorrect cart totals at checkout (APP-003) across NA and EU (Sev1). Root cause was the systemic absence of write-through/event-driven cache coherence between Pricing (APP-007) and the promo cache; prior path-by-path patches were insufficient. Resolved by implementing a systemic write-through invalidation and adding a standing pre-release promotion-window cache-invalidation check; codified in KN-063 and the ARCH-05 systemic-pattern example.

title: Postmortem: Checkout p99 latency regression from synchronous promo call
body: REL-2026-010 added a synchronous Promotions Engine call on the Checkout Service (APP-003) critical path, adding its tail latency to checkout p99 and breaching the latency SLO under load in NA. Root cause was capacity/latency-budget: an unbudgeted synchronous hop on a latency-sensitive Tier 0 path. Fixed in 8 minutes by making the promotions call asynchronous behind a flag; follow-ups enforce a checkout critical-path latency budget and add a performance gate.

title: Postmortem: Catalog ingestion stalled on data-platform outage
body: A brief Enterprise Data Platform (APP-020) outage stalled the Product Catalog (APP-005) offer-ingestion pipeline for ~14 minutes, briefly staling new offer data across NA, EU and APAC. Root cause was an upstream dependency failure; Catalog degraded gracefully by serving last-known-good data and resumed ingestion on recovery with no data loss. Resolved when APP-020 recovered and the backlog drained; follow-ups define an offer-freshness SLO and add a downstream-visible freshness indicator.
